context.process_name: Debt Investment Economics: Loan Workbook, Yields, PIK, OID & Warrants
context.objective: Document how we carry out Debt Investment Economics: Loan Workbook, Yields, PIK, OID & Warrants, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: What starts this work?

I tend to think about this one from the back end, so let me start there. The last thing that happens each month is the period close: I am the workbook preparer, and together with the independent checker we reconcile everything, get a record of the checker's review, and then lock and version the loan workbook for that period. We do not close until principal, income, cash, amortization and the GL and trial balance show zero unexplained difference.

Going back to your actual question, what starts it. The very first build of a loan workbook starts when the client completes a debt investment and we at GPFS receive the final executed loan documents. The purchase and setup process, FA-09, has to be complete before I begin. After that first build the work recurs every month for interest and amortization recognition, and the cash activity tends to bunch up around month-end and the start of the month. It also gets kicked off by events in between: a new draw or tranche, an amendment, a rate change, a borrower cash or PIK election, a default, a prepayment, an exit fee or make-whole event, a warrant allocation, or a change in maturity.
Talk me through how you build and update the loan workbook after a new investment or monthly close begins?

The part people picture is the calculations, so I will start there and then back up. For each period I calculate cash interest as the contractual principal times the cash rate times the contractual day-count fraction, using only the rate, basis and dates in the agreement. I never default to Actual/360 unless the executed terms say so. Then I calculate PIK interest on the contractual principal base and add it to principal on the contractual capitalization date, and the increased principal feeds the later cash and PIK calculations. The roll-forward I hold to is ending principal equals opening principal plus draws minus repayments plus PIK plus approved adjustments. I also build the OID and warrant amortization, which is a straight-line schedule from the start date to maturity, and the cumulative amortization has to equal the total allocated warrant cost by maturity.

But none of that happens first. For a new investment I start by creating one controlled workbook for that investment in Excel plus a setup checklist, and I record the fund, borrower, issuer or security, investment date, original principal, currency, maturity and document version. I assign an independent checker at that point and list any special features, like PIK, a toggle, warrants, default, exit fee, make-whole, draws, amendments or conversion. Next I validate the executed document set: I confirm the documents are final and executed and for the right parties, inventory the agreement, schedules, notes, warrant documents, side letters, funding notices and amendments, and log anything missing, draft or conflicting. The checker confirms the set is complete. Then I record all the loan terms in the contract-term checklist and cite the document section and page for every material term, and the checker records the material terms separately and we compare.

After that I reconcile opening principal to cash and accounting. In a recurring month that means carrying forward the prior ending principal, accrued cash interest, cumulative PIK and the OID or warrant balance from the prior locked workbook, and if there is an unexplained opening difference I pause the current period. Only then do I lay out the schedule, period by period from inception through contractual maturity with no gaps or overlaps, and I show stub periods explicitly instead of forcing them into a standard period.
When the document review finds something missing or conflicting, what happens before you proceed with the workbook?

Where it ends up is that the affected calculation sits on hold. If a term is unresolved or two amendments conflict, I do not calculate that piece until it is settled, and I only pick it back up once I have written direction in hand.

Backing up to what I do first: I log the missing, draft or conflicting document in the document checklist and go back to the client or investment team, because they are the ones who provide the final executed documents and clarify the terms. I will not take an economic term from a draft or from an unsupported email when executed support should exist. If the thing that is unclear is a day-count method or a rate term, the independent checker decides how it should be read and gives me that in writing, and in the meantime I do not fall back on Actual/360. Everything that does not depend on the open item can keep moving, but the affected work stays stopped until the record and approval are complete.
When an opening balance difference is unexplained, what do you do to resolve it before resuming the period?

First, I need to fix something. I misspoke earlier: it is the client or their legal counsel who decides how an unclear day-count method or rate term should be read, not the independent checker. The checker reviews my work but does not make that call. I wait for written direction from the client or legal counsel.

On the opening difference, the finish line is that the checker verifies the opening reconciliation and there is zero unexplained difference in principal and in the cumulative income and amortization balances. I do not start the current period's calculations until then.

To get there I go back through the pieces. I reconcile the original and any later funded principal to the cash records and to accounting. I compare what I carried forward against the prior locked workbook, meaning prior ending principal, accrued cash interest, cumulative PIK and the OID or warrant balance. And I reconcile the prior period's income summary to what was actually posted in the GL and the trial balance. Every difference I find is either resolved or documented before I move on. If I cannot correct it myself I escalate it instead of letting dependent work go ahead, and the opening reconciliation is kept as the record. We do this check every period, not just at setup.
Who takes an opening-difference escalation and determines how it is resolved?

Let me say where it lands at the close first, because that part I do know. At the monthly or period close every open variance has to be either resolved or assigned to someone, and if it is not, we keep the period open or explicitly document it as an owned exception. We never overwrite an unresolved item just to get the workbook closed.

As for who actually takes the escalation and decides how an opening difference gets resolved, I do not know. Nobody has been formally named as the process owner or the accountable approver for this work, and even the preparer and checker role titles have not been confirmed. The service-line governance owner is the person who would have to confirm that.

What I can tell you is who touches the pieces. The Accounting or Fund Team maintain the GL, the trial balance and the investment records, and they escalate differences in posting, accounts, balances or reconciliations before close. The Treasury or cash-monitoring role gives me the actual cash receipt detail. So in practice I work the difference with them, but who has the final say is not something I can point to.
How do you learn that an investment event, such as an amendment or new draw, needs a workbook update?

I will give you the end of an update first, since that is what makes it count. An amendment or draw update is not done until I have compared the before and after values and have the checker's approval record on that comparison. Stub and amendment formula errors are one of the biggest risks we have, so posting is held until the formulas have been checked.

Now, how I find out. The executed amendment or the draw notice comes to me from the client or investment team, and they are the ones who confirm borrower events. For a cash or PIK election it is the borrower's notice. I need the executed amendment or draw notice and the prior controlled workbook in hand before I touch anything. The other way I know something is coming is my own close routine: at each period close I record the upcoming payment, maturity, toggle, amendment and monitoring dates, so those are on my radar for the next period.

Once I have the executed support, the order is this. I keep a controlled copy and version of the schedule as it stood before the change. I record the changed principal, rates, dates, maturity, toggle, fees and warrant allocation. I insert a split or stub period at the exact effective date, update principal and rates from that date, and check that the later periods realign to the contractual dates. Then I update the cash, PIK, OID and warrant, fee and income summary sections, and that is when the before and after comparison goes to the checker.
What does the checker verify in the before-and-after comparison?

What the checker's approval releases is the posting, so I will start there. Once the change is approved, the updated amounts flow into the monthly income summary. I prepare that summary, the checker reviews it, and the Accounting or Fund Team post the entry after review. The before and after comparison is the gate in front of all that.

Going back to what the checker actually verifies in the comparison, it is two things. One, every changed term and its effective date can be traced to executed support. Two, nothing is missing or duplicated across the change: no days, no principal, no allocations and no income. That second one is where split and stub periods bite, because it is easy to count a day twice or drop one at the effective date.

If the check fails, the affected work stops and I correct it or escalate it. In practice that means splitting the stub period at the effective date again and revalidating all the later periods. We do this check for every amendment and every draw, and the before and after comparison itself is kept as the record.
How do you determine the yield used in the loan workbook?

Let me answer from the far end, where the rates get tested. Late in the month the system side runs in Alta Return, which we also call Allvue NAV. That is not me, it is an assigned system and accrual preparer. They set Security Type and Debt Type to Loan, and set Calculation Type to Payment Date for a PIK security or Accrual for a non-PIK one. For a PIK security they do not use First Compounding Date. Then they run Security Filter, then Suggest Lines, and review the journal entry lines it populates. Those suggested lines have to agree to my Excel schedule except for documented, approved rounding. If there is an unexplained difference between Allvue and Excel, it is not posted and the submission is held. What the rounding tolerance is, I do not know. That has not been confirmed, and the system owner would have to say.

Going back to your question, I do not pick a yield. What the loan earns in the workbook comes straight from the contract. The cash rate and the PIK rate come from the executed credit agreement and its amendments, and I capture the effective dates, tiers, floors, spreads and default provisions and how they change over time. I never take a rate from a worked example or from another client's workbook. The Machine Metrics and Omega Point examples are references, not rules.

The other piece of the return is the warrant cost allocation that we group with OID. The approved allocated cost is amortized straight-line to maturity and that amortization goes into income each month. The exact convention for that, daily or monthly, the rounding and how later draws are layered in, has not been confirmed, so I cannot tell you. The accounting or audit process expert is who would confirm it.
Where does the approved allocated warrant cost come from?

The place that number really gets tested is at the end of the loan, so I will start there. If the loan pays off early, I separately identify whatever warrant or OID amount is still unamortized, and I get accounting and client approval for how the realized gain or loss is treated before anything is recorded.

Going back to where the number comes from in the first place: I do not value the warrant. Valuation is outside this process. The allocated cost comes to me from the executed or approved deal and accounting support, and what I do is confirm the allocation date, the amount, which draws or tranches it relates to, and the approved accounting method. The client's tax or accounting adviser owns the conclusion on OID and warrant treatment.

In the workbook I record each allocated cost by inception or by draw and aggregate them, but I keep the tranche-level support so each allocation traces back to approved support. If a later draw comes with its own warrant allocation, I add the supported allocation as a separate amortization layer, and the client or their accounting adviser decides that treatment. I keep the allocation support and the schedule as the record.
You said close requires zero unexplained differences, but also that an open variance can be documented as an owned exception; how does an owned exception affect whether the period can close?
This capture still has open sections. 15 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.

notes.summary: Allocated warrant cost comes from approved deal and accounting support, not valuation within this process. Later-draw allocations are separately layered. Early-payoff gain or loss treatment requires accounting and client approval before recording; detailed amortization conventions remain unconfirmed.

steps.title: Receive executed loan documents
steps.description: The first workbook build starts when GPFS receives the final executed loan documents after the client completes a debt investment.

steps.title: Complete purchase and setup
steps.description: The upstream purchase and setup process, FA-09, must be complete before the preparer begins the first build. Its internal work is not described.

steps.title: Create controlled loan workbook
steps.description: For a new investment, create one controlled workbook and a setup checklist. Record the investment details, assign an independent checker, and list special features.

steps.title: Start monthly recognition
steps.description: After the first build, the work recurs monthly for interest and amortization recognition.

steps.title: Recognize interest and amortization
steps.description: Monthly work includes interest and amortization recognition. The calculation, recording and handoff are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Investment event occurs
steps.description: Events include draws, amendments, rate changes, borrower elections, defaults, prepayments, exit fees, make-whole events, warrant allocations and maturity changes. Amendment and draw updates are described; the routes for other events remain partly UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Reconcile period-close balances
steps.description: At monthly or period close, the preparer and checker reconcile principal, income, cash, amortization, the GL and trial balance. Open variances must be resolved or assigned; the relationship between owned exceptions and the zero-unexplained-difference close requirement is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Obtain checker review record
steps.description: A record of the independent checker's review is obtained before the workbook is locked and versioned. Who records it and where it is retained are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Lock and version workbook
steps.description: The loan workbook is locked and versioned for the period after reconciliation and the review record. Close requires zero unexplained difference across the stated balances.

steps.title: Validate loan document set
steps.description: Confirm documents are final, executed, and for the right parties; inventory the reported document types; log missing, draft, or conflicting items.

steps.title: Confirm document set completeness
steps.description: The checker confirms that the document set is complete.

steps.title: Record contract terms
steps.description: Record loan terms in the contract-term checklist, citing the document section and page for every material term. Capture cash and PIK rates and their effective dates, tiers, floors, spreads and default provisions as they change over time.

steps.title: Compare recorded material terms
steps.description: The checker records material terms separately, and the checker and preparer compare their records.

steps.title: Reconcile opening balances
steps.description: Each period, reconcile funded principal to cash and accounting, compare carried-forward balances with the prior locked workbook, and reconcile prior income to the GL and trial balance. Resolve or document differences and escalate those the preparer cannot correct; the preparer works differences with Accounting or Fund Team and Treasury or cash monitoring.

steps.title: Carry forward prior balances
steps.description: For a recurring month, carry forward prior ending principal, accrued cash interest, cumulative PIK and the OID or warrant balance from the prior locked workbook.

steps.title: Lay out period schedule
steps.description: Lay out periods from inception through contractual maturity without gaps or overlaps, showing stub periods explicitly.

steps.title: Calculate cash interest
steps.description: For each period, calculate contractual principal multiplied by the cash rate and contractual day-count fraction, using the agreement's rate, basis, and dates.

steps.title: Calculate and capitalize PIK
steps.description: Calculate PIK interest on the contractual principal base and add it to principal on the contractual capitalization date. Increased principal feeds later cash and PIK calculations.

steps.title: Calculate principal roll-forward
steps.description: Calculate ending principal from opening principal, draws, repayments, PIK, and approved adjustments.

steps.title: Build amortization schedules
steps.description: Build straight-line OID and warrant amortization to maturity and include approved warrant-cost amortization in monthly income. Later-draw allocations are separate layers, but the detailed daily or monthly convention, rounding and layering method remain unconfirmed.

steps.title: Wait on opening differences
steps.description: Pause current-period calculations when an opening difference is unexplained. Differences are resolved or documented for checker verification; calculations remain held until the checker verifies the reconciliation and the stated balances have zero unexplained difference.

steps.title: Seek documents or clarification
steps.description: Go back to the client or investment team for final executed documents or clarification. Do not take an economic term from a draft or unsupported email when executed support should exist.

steps.title: Hold affected calculation
steps.description: An unresolved term or conflicting amendments hold the affected calculation. Work not dependent on the open item can continue.

steps.title: Interpret unclear rate or basis
steps.description: The client or legal counsel decides how an unclear day-count method or rate term should be read. The preparer waits for written direction; the independent checker reviews the preparer's work but does not make the interpretation.

steps.title: Verify opening reconciliation
steps.description: Verify the opening reconciliation. Current-period calculations cannot start until the checker has verified it and principal and cumulative income and amortization balances have zero unexplained difference.

steps.title: Escalate uncorrectable difference
steps.description: Escalate an opening difference the preparer cannot correct rather than allowing dependent work to proceed. The preparer works differences with Accounting or Fund Team and Treasury or cash monitoring, but the escalation recipient and final decision-maker are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Provide cash receipt detail
steps.description: Provide the preparer with actual cash receipt detail. Its precise placement in the process is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Handle unowned close variance
steps.description: If an open variance is not resolved or assigned at close, keep the period open or explicitly document it as an owned exception. Do not overwrite an unresolved item to close the workbook.

steps.title: Escalate accounting differences
steps.system: GL, trial balance and investment records; systems UNKNOWN
steps.description: The Accounting or Fund Team maintains the GL, trial balance and investment records and escalates differences in posting, accounts, balances or reconciliations before close. The recipient and subsequent handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Receive amendment or draw notice
steps.description: Receive the executed amendment or draw notice from the client or investment team, who also confirm borrower events.

steps.title: Preserve pre-change schedule
steps.description: Keep a controlled copy and version of the schedule as it stood before the change.

steps.title: Record changed investment terms
steps.description: Record changed principal, rates, dates, maturity, toggle, fees and warrant allocation.

steps.title: Update effective-date schedule
steps.description: Insert a split or stub period at the exact effective date, update principal and rates from that date, and check that later periods realign to contractual dates.

steps.title: Update economics sections
steps.description: Update the cash, PIK, OID and warrant, fee and income summary sections.

steps.title: Compare before and after values
steps.description: Compare the before and after values and send the comparison to the checker.

steps.title: Obtain comparison approval record
steps.description: Obtain the checker's approval record on the before-and-after comparison. Approval is required to complete the amendment or draw update and releases the subsequent summary and posting route.

steps.title: Receive borrower election notice
steps.description: For a cash or PIK election, the preparer learns of the event from the borrower's notice. The subsequent route is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Record upcoming monitoring dates
steps.description: At each period close, record upcoming payment, maturity, toggle, amendment and monitoring dates for the next period.

steps.title: Check formulas before posting
steps.description: Posting is held until formulas have been checked. Stub and amendment formula errors are a major reported risk; the checker and exact placement of this formula check are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Check change comparison
steps.description: Check that changed terms and effective dates trace to executed support, and that no days, principal, allocations or income are missing or duplicated. The comparison is retained; its location is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Correct failed change check
steps.description: When the check fails, stop affected work and correct it. The reported correction involves splitting the stub at the effective date again and revalidating later periods.

steps.title: Prepare monthly income summary
steps.description: After change approval, prepare the monthly income summary using the updated amounts.

steps.title: Review income summary
steps.description: Review the preparer's monthly income summary. The specific checks and handling of a failed review are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Post income entry
steps.description: Post the entry after summary review. For the reported amendment or draw route, change approval and the formula check are also required before posting.

steps.title: Escalate failed change check
steps.description: Escalate a failed comparison check as an alternative to correcting it. Affected work remains stopped; recipient and subsequent handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Set loan calculation types
steps.system: Alta Return, also called Allvue NAV
steps.description: Late in the month, set Security Type and Debt Type to Loan. Set Calculation Type to Payment Date for a PIK security or Accrual for a non-PIK security; do not use First Compounding Date for a PIK security.

steps.title: Run Security Filter
steps.description: Run Security Filter after setting the reported loan and calculation types.

steps.title: Run Suggest Lines
steps.description: Run Suggest Lines to populate journal entry lines.

steps.title: Review suggested journal lines
steps.description: Review the populated journal entry lines. They must agree to the Excel schedule except for documented, approved rounding; the rounding tolerance is unconfirmed.

steps.title: Hold unmatched submission
steps.description: Hold the submission and do not post when an Allvue-to-Excel difference is unexplained. The resolution process and subsequent handoff are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Confirm warrant allocation support
steps.description: Confirm the allocation date, amount, related draws or tranches and approved accounting method from executed or approved deal and accounting support. Valuation is outside this process; the client's tax or accounting adviser owns the OID and warrant treatment conclusion.

steps.title: Record allocated warrant costs
steps.description: Record and aggregate allocated costs by inception or draw. Keep tranche-level support so each allocation traces to approved support; retain the support and schedule.

steps.title: Determine later-draw treatment
steps.description: Decide the treatment of a later draw with its own warrant allocation. The timing and how the decision is communicated or recorded are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Add later-draw allocation layer
steps.description: When a later draw has its own warrant allocation, add the supported allocation as a separate amortization layer. The detailed layering convention is unconfirmed.

steps.title: Identify unamortized payoff amount
steps.description: If the loan pays off early, separately identify the remaining unamortized warrant or OID amount.

steps.title: Obtain payoff treatment approvals
steps.actor: Workbook preparer; accounting and client approvers
steps.description: Obtain accounting and client approval for the realized gain or loss treatment before anything is recorded. The approval sequence, records and subsequent recording action are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Receive executed loan documents
steps.description: The first workbook build starts when GPFS receives final executed loan documents after the client completes a debt investment.

steps.title: Complete purchase and setup
steps.description: FA-09 purchase and setup must be complete before the first build. Its internal actions and readiness notification are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Create controlled loan workbook
steps.description: For a new investment, create one controlled workbook and a setup checklist. Record fund, borrower, issuer or security, investment date, original principal, currency, maturity and document version. Assign an independent checker and list applicable special features, including PIK, toggle, warrants, default, exit fee, make-whole, draws, amendments or conversion.

steps.title: Validate loan document set
steps.description: Confirm the documents are final, executed and for the right parties. Inventory the agreement, schedules, notes, warrant documents, side letters, funding notices and amendments. Log missing, draft or conflicting items in the document checklist.

steps.title: Confirm document set completeness
steps.description: Confirm that the document set is complete. How this confirmation operates when an item remains open is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Seek documents or clarification
steps.description: Go back to the client or investment team for final executed documents or clarification. Do not take an economic term from a draft or unsupported email when executed support should exist.

steps.title: Hold affected calculation
steps.description: Hold the calculation affected by an unresolved term or conflicting amendments. Work that does not depend on the open item can continue. Pick the affected work back up only with written direction in hand and the record and approval complete.

steps.title: Interpret unclear rate or basis
steps.description: The client or legal counsel decides how to read an unclear rate or day-count term; the preparer waits for written direction. The checker reviews the work but does not make that interpretation. Do not default to Actual/360 while waiting.

steps.title: Record and compare contract terms
steps.description: The preparer records loan terms in the contract-term checklist, citing the document section and page for every material term. Capture cash and PIK rates, effective dates, tiers, floors, spreads and default provisions as they change over time. The checker separately records material terms and compares them with the preparer. Resolution of differences is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Start monthly recognition
steps.description: After the first build, work recurs monthly for interest and amortization recognition. Cash activity tends to bunch around month-end and the start of the month.

steps.title: Carry forward prior balances
steps.description: For a recurring month, carry forward prior ending principal, accrued cash interest, cumulative PIK and the OID or warrant balance from the prior locked workbook.

steps.title: Reconcile opening balances
steps.description: Each period, reconcile original and later funded principal to cash and accounting; compare carried-forward balances with the prior locked workbook; and reconcile the prior income summary to postings in the GL and trial balance. Resolve or document every difference. Retain the opening reconciliation. The preparer works differences with Accounting or Fund Team and Treasury or cash monitoring.

steps.title: Escalate opening difference
steps.description: Escalate a difference the preparer cannot correct, rather than allowing dependent work to proceed. The recipient, final decision-maker and return route are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Verify opening reconciliation
steps.description: Verify the opening reconciliation. Current-period calculations do not start until verification and zero unexplained difference in principal and cumulative income and amortization balances.

steps.title: Lay out period schedule
steps.description: Lay out the schedule period by period from inception through contractual maturity, without gaps or overlaps. Show stub periods explicitly rather than forcing them into standard periods.

steps.title: Calculate cash and PIK interest
steps.description: For each period calculate cash interest as contractual principal times cash rate times the contractual day-count fraction, using the agreement's rate, basis and dates. Do not default to Actual/360 unless executed terms say so. Calculate PIK on the contractual principal base and add it to principal on the contractual capitalization date; increased principal feeds later cash and PIK calculations.

steps.title: Calculate principal roll-forward
steps.description: Ending principal equals opening principal plus draws minus repayments plus PIK plus approved adjustments. How adjustments are approved and the detailed sequence of this calculation are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Confirm warrant allocation support
steps.description: Confirm allocation date, amount, related draws or tranches and approved accounting method using executed or approved deal and accounting support. Warrant valuation is outside this process. The client's tax or accounting adviser owns the OID and warrant treatment conclusion.

steps.title: Record allocated warrant costs
steps.description: Record each allocated cost by inception or draw and aggregate the costs. Keep tranche-level support so each allocation traces to approved support; retain the allocation support and schedule.

steps.title: Build amortization schedules
steps.description: Build straight-line OID and warrant amortization from start date to maturity. Approved allocated warrant cost amortization goes into monthly income; cumulative amortization must equal total allocated warrant cost by maturity. The daily or monthly convention, rounding and detailed layering method are unconfirmed.

steps.title: Investment event occurs
steps.description: Event-driven work can be triggered by a new draw or tranche, amendment, rate change, borrower cash or PIK election, default, prepayment, exit fee or make-whole event, warrant allocation or maturity change. Routes not described below remain UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Receive amendment or draw notice
steps.description: Receive the executed amendment or draw notice from the client or investment team, who confirm borrower events. Both the executed support and prior controlled workbook must be in hand before touching the update.

steps.title: Preserve pre-change schedule
steps.description: Keep a controlled copy and version of the schedule as it stood before the change.

steps.title: Record changed investment terms
steps.description: Record changed principal, rates, dates, maturity, toggle, fees and warrant allocation.

steps.title: Update effective-date schedule
steps.description: Insert a split or stub period at the exact effective date, update principal and rates from that date, and check that later periods realign to contractual dates.

steps.title: Update economics sections
steps.description: Update cash, PIK, OID and warrant, fee and income summary sections.

steps.title: Compare before and after values
steps.description: Compare before and after values and send the comparison to the checker. The comparison itself is retained.

steps.title: Does the change comparison pass?
steps.description: For every amendment and draw, verify that each changed term and effective date traces to executed support and that no days, principal, allocations or income are missing or duplicated. Failure stops affected work for correction or escalation; approval releases the posting route.

steps.title: Correct failed change check
steps.description: Stop affected work and correct a failed check. In practice, split the stub period again at the effective date and revalidate all later periods. The amendment or draw comparison still requires checker approval.

steps.title: Escalate failed change check
steps.description: Escalate a failed comparison check as an alternative to correcting it. Affected work remains stopped. Recipient and subsequent handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Obtain comparison approval record
steps.actor: Workbook preparer obtains checker approval; record keeper UNKNOWN
steps.description: Obtain the checker's approval record on the comparison. An amendment or draw update is not complete without that record. Approval releases the subsequent posting route.

steps.title: Prepare monthly income summary
steps.description: After change approval, prepare the monthly income summary using updated amounts. Approved allocated warrant cost amortization also goes into income monthly.

steps.title: Review income summary
steps.description: Review the monthly income summary. Specific checks and failed-review handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Check formulas before posting
steps.description: Posting is held until formulas have been checked. Stub and amendment formula errors are a major reported risk. The performer, precise placement, checks and failure handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Post income entry
steps.description: Post the entry after summary review. For the reported amendment or draw route, the change comparison must also be approved and formulas checked before posting.

steps.title: Receive borrower election notice
steps.description: For a cash or PIK election, learn of the event from the borrower's notice. Subsequent handling is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Add later-draw allocation layer
steps.description: If a later draw has its own warrant allocation, add the supported allocation as a separate amortization layer. The client or its accounting adviser decides that treatment. Decision timing and detailed layering convention are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Identify unamortized payoff amount
steps.description: If the loan pays off early, separately identify the remaining unamortized warrant or OID amount.

steps.title: Obtain payoff treatment approvals
steps.actor: Workbook preparer; accounting and client approvers
steps.description: Obtain both accounting and client approval of realized gain or loss treatment before anything is recorded. Approval order, retained evidence and subsequent recording action are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Set loan calculation types
steps.system: Alta Return, also called Allvue NAV
steps.description: Late in the month set Security Type and Debt Type to Loan. Set Calculation Type to Payment Date for a PIK security or Accrual for a non-PIK security. Do not use First Compounding Date for a PIK security.

steps.title: Run Security Filter
steps.description: Run Security Filter after applying the reported settings.

steps.title: Run Suggest Lines
steps.description: Run Suggest Lines to populate journal entry lines.

steps.title: Review suggested journal lines
steps.system: Alta Return / Allvue NAV and Excel
steps.description: Review populated journal lines against the Excel schedule. They must agree except for documented, approved rounding. The tolerance, rounding approver and resolution procedure are unconfirmed.

steps.title: Hold unmatched submission
steps.description: When the Allvue-to-Excel difference is unexplained, hold submission and do not post. Resolution and release are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Reconcile period-close balances
steps.description: At monthly or period close, reconcile principal, income, cash, amortization, GL and trial balance. The participant reports that close requires zero unexplained difference. Every open variance must be resolved or assigned; how an owned exception affects the close condition is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Handle unowned close variance
steps.description: If an open variance is neither resolved nor assigned, keep the period open or explicitly document it as an owned exception. Do not overwrite an unresolved item to close the workbook. The subsequent route and effect on close are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Obtain checker review record
steps.description: Obtain a record of the independent checker's review before locking and versioning the workbook. The recorder and storage location are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Lock and version workbook
steps.description: Lock and version the workbook for the period after reconciliation and the checker review record. The reported close condition is zero unexplained difference; the effect of an owned exception remains unresolved.

steps.title: Record upcoming monitoring dates
steps.description: At each period close, record upcoming payment, maturity, toggle, amendment and monitoring dates for the next period. Exact placement within close and storage are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Escalate accounting differences
steps.description: The Accounting or Fund Team maintains the GL, trial balance and investment records and escalates differences in posting, accounts, balances or reconciliations before close. Recipient and subsequent handling are UNKNOWN.

topics.answer: The intake calls the work Debt Investment Economics: Loan Workbook, Yields, PIK, OID and Warrants. The participant describes controlled loan workbook setup, calculations, changes and close. Other process names are UNKNOWN; Alta Return is also called Allvue NAV.

The work produces a controlled loan workbook and monthly income information reflecting contractual debt economics, with reconciled and versioned period records. The full recipient and downstream value are UNKNOWN.

The first build starts after a client completes a debt investment and GPFS receives final executed documents; FA-09 must also be complete. Work recurs monthly and is triggered by draws, amendments, rate changes, elections and other investment events. The client or investment team sends amendment and draw support; borrower notices communicate elections. Fixed deadlines and monthly-cycle detection are UNKNOWN.

At close, the preparer and checker reconcile specified balances, obtain a checker review record and lock and version the workbook. Zero unexplained differences are reported as necessary, but how an owned exception affects close is UNKNOWN. The prior locked workbook supplies next-period balances; other consumers are UNKNOWN.

No process owner or accountable approver has been formally named. The participant is the workbook preparer and an independent checker reviews the work, but even those role titles are unconfirmed. The service-line governance owner would confirm them.

The preparer creates a controlled Excel workbook and checklist, validates executed documents, records terms with citations and compares them with the checker's separate record. Opening balances are reconciled and verified each period before current-period calculations. The preparer lays out schedules, calculates cash and PIK and builds amortization. Changes are versioned, updated and compared for checker approval before summary review and posting. A separate Allvue accrual route reviews suggested lines against Excel, and close reconciles and versions the workbook. Some links, exception exits and downstream handoffs remain UNKNOWN.

The checker confirms document completeness, independently records terms, verifies the opening reconciliation and checks changed terms, dates and omissions or duplication. Change approval and formula checking gate posting; the checker reviews the income summary. Allvue lines must agree to Excel except for approved documented rounding, and close requires a review record. Early-payoff treatment needs accounting and client approval before recording. Evidence locations, some failure routes, thresholds and system enforcement are UNKNOWN.

PIK securities use Payment Date and no First Compounding Date in Allvue; non-PIK securities use Accrual.
